scenes.tagline: Invoice financing for African exporters. Get paid when you ship, not when your buyer pays.
scenes.tag: Arbitrum Open House Singapore · Robinhood Chain · Paxos USDG
scenes.vo: This is EarnX: invoice financing for African exporters, on Robinhood Chain and Arbitrum.

scenes.label: Why I'm building this
scenes.head: My mother, Mama Dora, grows cassava and other crops in Delta State, Nigeria.

bullets.v: The most to show, and the least cash in hand.
The hospital needed money that week.
Fees and interest that bankrupted us.

scenes.vo: My mother, Mama Dora, grows cassava and other crops in Delta State, Nigeria. Just after harvest, my father had a stroke, and the hospital needed money that week. Her harvest was worth more than the bill, but it wasn't cash yet. We sold crops cheaply, then borrowed from a bank, and the fees and interest bankrupted us.

scenes.label: The gap
scenes.head: Millions of African exporters hit the same wall.

bullets.v: of trade finance requested by African businesses went unmet in 2024 (AfDB).
of trade finance applications from African firms, 2020 to 2024 (AfDB).

scenes.vo: Millions of African exporters hit the same wall. In 2024, seventy-four to ninety-two billion dollars of their trade finance requests went unmet.

scenes.label: Bank versus EarnX
scenes.head: A sixty-day invoice: about 7% at a Nigerian bank, about 3% on EarnX.

bullets.v: 29.2% a year (CBN, Aug 2026), up to 2% in fees, collateral, weeks of waiting.
12.35% a year for the term, plus 1% to the reserve. No collateral.
In the transaction that completes the funding.

scenes.vo: For a sixty-day invoice, a Nigerian bank costs about seven percent, plus collateral and weeks of waiting. EarnX costs about three, paid out the moment it's funded.

scenes.label: How EarnX works
scenes.head: An invoice becomes an on-chain asset.

bullets.v: Invoice and documents; their hash goes on-chain.
Checks, a Rust engine sets the terms, the buyer signs.
Investors fund in USDG; the exporter is paid at once.
The buyer pays; investors claim pro-rata.

diagram.note: Investors claim principal plus yield, pro-rata.

scenes.vo: Here's the flow: priced on-chain by a Rust engine, confirmed by the buyer, funded in USDG, repaid, and claimed.

scenes.head: Live on Robinhood Chain and Arbitrum
scenes.sub: Every number is read from the contracts; the globe draws each invoice's route.
scenes.vo: It's live on both chains, and every number on screen is read from the contracts.

scenes.head: An exporter signs in with a passkey
scenes.sub: No wallet app, no seed phrase, no gas: a ZeroDev smart account with sponsored fees.
scenes.vo: An exporter signs in with a passkey: no wallet app, no seed phrase, no gas, thanks to a ZeroDev smart account.

scenes.head: Invoice and documents, submitted on-chain
scenes.sub: The documents go to IPFS; the invoice, its number and their hash go on Robinhood Chain.
scenes.vo: She enters the shipment and her invoice number, attaches the invoice and bill of lading, and submits. The documents go to IPFS; their hash goes on-chain.

scenes.head: Checked, priced in Rust, sent to the buyer
scenes.sub: Hash match, no duplicate on either chain, the $1,000 limit for unverified exporters, then the Stylus engine sets the APR.
scenes.vo: Seconds later it's verified: documents match, no duplicate on either chain, within the limit for unverified exporters, and our Rust Stylus contract sets the yield. Then she sends her buyer a link.

scenes.head: Her deal sheet: who stands behind it
scenes.sub: Business verification status, buyer confirmation, pricing line by line, and her soulbound record.
scenes.vo: Still signed in, she sees her deal sheet: who stands behind it, the pricing line by line, and a soulbound token minted as her record.

scenes.head: The buyer confirms the debt
scenes.sub: A statement built from the on-chain facts, signed by the buyer's wallet or passkey, pinned to IPFS.
scenes.vo: Her buyer opens the link, reads exactly what they're signing, and confirms with one signature, pinned to IPFS for every investor to check.

scenes.head: Buyer confirmed, so an investor funds it
scenes.sub: The investment completes the funding, pays the exporter and sends 1% to the reserve, in one transaction.
scenes.vo: An investor sees the buyer has confirmed and funds it in USDG. That one transaction pays the exporter about forty dollars and turns her token to funded.

scenes.head: The buyer repays
scenes.sub: Principal plus the invoice's APR for its term.
scenes.vo: When the buyer pays, principal plus yield lands on-chain, and her token reads repaid.

scenes.head: Investors claim principal plus yield
scenes.sub: 40.50 USDG in, 40.91 back: 12.2% a year for 30 days, paid pro-rata.
scenes.vo: The investor claims forty ninety-one for forty and a half: twelve percent a year, for thirty days.

scenes.head: Every step is public
scenes.sub: Robinhood Chain's explorer: the investor's USDG in, the exporter's payout out, then the buyer's repayment.
scenes.vo: Every step is public: on Robinhood Chain's explorer, the investor's USDG goes in, her payout comes out, and the buyer's repayment follows.

scenes.head: A credit history she owns
scenes.sub: A non-transferable record no one can buy, sell or fake.
scenes.vo: Her page now shows a repaid invoice: a credit history she owns, that no one can buy, sell or fake.

scenes.head: Tested like it holds real money
scenes.sub: 29 Foundry tests including fuzzing, 6 Rust tests for the engine, CI on every push.
scenes.vo: Twenty-nine Foundry tests, including fuzzing, and six Rust tests for the engine run on every push.

scenes.label: Model, traction, next
scenes.head: Live on two testnets. Every transaction is public.

bullets.v: 1% of each advance funds the investors' reserve; an EarnX origination fee comes next.
36 invoices on two testnets, samples and tests so far; 5 repaid in full.
A licensed identity partner for business checks, then our first real exporters.

scenes.vo: One percent of each advance funds the reserve; an origination fee comes next. Thirty-six invoices so far, five repaid. Next: a licensed identity partner, then real exporters.
